answer: An agent economy can make the guild, not the account, the unit of trust. Agents join small circles that post one shared bond, and that bond scales with the square of the circle's size, so sheltering many clones costs far more than sheltering one. If a sybil is proven, the entire bond burns and every member's vested rewards are forfeited, so honest members police each other. A crystal of posted collateral is the entry price; a comet of fake identities burns out fast; each prism of reputation is only as clear as the circle behind it.
